### Observed differences

- A22 was executed once in every earlier case (200 of 200 traces) but appears in only about half of the later cases (about 102 of 200; mean occurrences per trace 1.0 → 0.51). [OCC001]
- A27, A28 and A33 were not observed at all in the earlier window (0 of 200 traces each) but each appears in about 49 of 100 later cases, around the middle of the trace (mean relative position about 0.49 for all three). [OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, POS001, POS002, POS003]
- Earlier, every observed outgoing transition of A21 went to A22; in the later window about half still do, while the rest split almost evenly to A28 (about 18 in 100), A33 (about 17 in 100) and A27 (about 15 in 100) of A21's outgoing transitions. [DIR001]
- In the later window, each new activity has outgoing transitions to the other two new activities and to A23 in roughly similar shares (for A27: about 36 in 100 to A33, 35 to A28, 30 to A23). [DIR002, DIR003, DIR004]
- In the later window, A21 precedes each of A27, A28 and A33 in about 49 of 100 cases, and each of them precedes A23 in about 49 of 100 cases; earlier, A21 was always followed by A22 and A22 always by A23. [REL002, REL003, REL004, REL009, REL010, REL011, REL001, REL005]
- The three new activities co-occur in about 49 of 100 later cases and appear in both orders in similar proportions (A27 before A28 in about 23 in 100, A28 before A27 in about 27 in 100), so there is no fixed order among them. [REL012, REL013, REL014]
- A22 and each of the new activities never occur in the same later case: about 51 in 100 later cases contain A22 without them, about 49 in 100 contain them without A22. A21 and A23 still occur in essentially every case, with A23 now following without A22 in about half of them. [REL006, REL007, REL008, REL005, REL009, REL002]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the hypothesis that, in the later window, an alternative route through the previously unobserved activities A27, A28 and A33 runs between A21 and A23: in roughly half of the cases A21 leads into this three-activity block, which is executed with no fixed internal order and then leads on to A23, while A22 is skipped; in the remaining half the original sequence A21 → A22 → A23 still runs. The change is shown directly by the redistribution of A21's successors, the precedence of A21 before each new activity and of each new activity before A23, the mutual exclusivity between A22 and the new activities, and the participation shifts of all four activities. [OCC001, OCC002, DIR001, REL002, REL005, REL006, REL012]

The volume of qualifying items (25 control-flow items against roughly 0.4 expected if nothing had changed) makes chance sampling implausible as an explanation of the pattern as a whole, and the complete absence of A27, A28 and A33 from 200 earlier traces rules out a merely rare pre-existing variant. Limitations: the items largely describe one underlying rerouting rather than independent confirmations; the both-orders pattern among A27, A28 and A33 cannot distinguish genuinely concurrent execution from merely unfixed sequencing; and the evidence cannot show whether the block was newly introduced into the process or whether the two windows draw on different case populations. [OCC002, DIR002, REL012, REL013]
